title: Model Quantization (AWQ/GGUF)
summary: Reduce model representation cost using hardware-compatible quantization while validating task quality, memory headroom, and actual serving speed.
overview: Model quantization represents weights, activations, or caches with reduced numerical precision. The exact target matters: weight-only quantization reduces stored model weight memory, while activation and cache quantization change different parts of the runtime. Lower bit width does not automatically produce faster inference unless the hardware and kernels efficiently support the representation.

AWQ is an activation-aware weight quantization method. GGUF is a model file format used by GGML-based runtimes and can carry several quantized tensor representations; it is not itself one quantization algorithm. Architects should distinguish the method, serialized artifact, runtime kernels, and calibration dataset when comparing deployments.

production.poc: A prototype compares the original and quantized model on target hardware using representative prompts and output checks.
production.production: Production versions calibration data, quantization settings, tokenizer, and runtime together, then tests long-context memory behavior.
production.scale: Enterprise scale maintains hardware-specific artifacts, slice-level quality thresholds, and rollback paths when precision changes affect sensitive task classes.

components.name: Calibration dataset
components.role: Represents the activation and language patterns expected in the deployment workload.

components.name: Quantization toolchain
components.role: Applies the selected method and records scales, grouping, and precision settings.

components.name: Artifact registry
components.role: Stores the quantized model with source-model lineage and format metadata.

components.name: Compatible runtime
components.role: Uses supported kernels for the chosen hardware and tensor representation.

components.name: Quality and performance harness
components.role: Compares outputs, memory, throughput, and latency against the baseline.

flow.title: Identify the bottleneck
flow.description: Determine whether weights, cache, bandwidth, or compute limit the deployment.

flow.title: Select compatible method
flow.description: Choose precision and quantization approach supported by the intended runtime and hardware.

flow.title: Calibrate and package
flow.description: Use representative data where required and preserve complete artifact lineage.

flow.title: Evaluate task quality
flow.description: Test extraction, reasoning, multilingual, and long-context slices relevant to the service.

flow.title: Benchmark serving behavior
flow.description: Measure real memory headroom and latency under the expected batch and context distribution.

flow.title: Deploy with rollback
flow.description: Canary the complete artifact-runtime pair and retain the previous precision configuration.

diagrams.caption: The deployment decision depends on measured task behavior and runtime support, not bit width alone.

useCase.title: Running a manual assistant on compact hardware
useCase.situation: A service team deploys an offline assistant on rugged workstations with limited accelerator memory.
useCase.problem: The full-precision model leaves insufficient room for the context needed to interpret service manuals.
useCase.requirement: Reduce weight memory while preserving part identifiers, units, and instruction conditions.
useCase.architecture: A quantized artifact is evaluated with the exact local runtime and a held-out service-question set.
runtime: The workstation loads the approved quantized bundle and runs representative long-context queries.
Quality gates compare identifier and condition fidelity against the higher-precision baseline.
useCase.failure: If a quantization setting corrupts numeric extraction, the deployment uses a less aggressive representation even if it consumes more memory.
useCase.impact: Measure accepted-answer quality, peak memory, startup, and latency; a smaller file does not prove a faster or adequate service.

tradeoffs.benefit: Reduces model storage and memory demand.
tradeoffs.cost: Can reduce quality or require specialized kernels.
May underrepresent rare domains or languages.

failures.detection: Runtime falls back and becomes slower than baseline.
failures.recovery: Verify actual kernel support and benchmark the chosen artifact.

failures.detection: Slice evaluation detects incorrect values despite stable average scores.
failures.recovery: Use higher precision or route that task to another evaluated model.

mistakes.fix: Separate file format from tensor precision and method.

mistakes.mistake: Assuming four bits means fourfold service savings
mistakes.fix: Include caches, activations, runtime overhead, and throughput.
Evaluate the deployment’s critical structured tasks.

whenToUse: Use when model memory limits deployment capacity.
Use when measured quality remains within the task contract.
whenNotToUse: Avoid aggressive precision reduction without task evaluation.
Do not assume all quantized formats are runtime-compatible.
Avoid optimizing file size while ignoring active-context memory.
checklist: Record method and artifact format separately.
Keep a validated precision rollback path.
